mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC is less than -0.10.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 500k signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC is not statistically significant at p<0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings expectations for industrial firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both the federal funds rate and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for two consecutive months signals a deflationary monetary easing, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% AND CPIAUCSL < 2% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above trend by more than 10% for four consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings and reduced marginal propensity to consume, which dampens demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and payrolls (PAYEMS) month-over-month indicates a paradoxical labor market where job creation is insufficient to absorb new entrants, foreshadowing wage pressure and inflation, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as markets anticipate higher corporate pricing power.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > previous month AND PAYEMS > previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 0.5% for six consecutive months signals a robust manufacturing expansion, which boosts earnings expectations for industrial firms and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change > 0.5% for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes (p > 0.05).
